renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: reconstructed_sunburst
  title: Reconstructed community by rank
  description: |-
    Each arc is a taxon of the reconstructed community, with kingdom in the centre and genus on the outside, sized by its read count and coloured by phylum. It answers which groups make up the community resolved across all amplified regions.
    How to read: wide arcs are the dominant taxa. A large share of arcs labelled Unclassified means the reference database could not name those sequences at that rank, so read the deeper ranks with care.
  kind: sunburst
  config:
    colour_by_rank: Phylum
  roles:
    ranks:
    - Kingdom
    - Phylum
    - Class
    - Genus
    abundance: count

- component: figure
  title: Composition by phylum
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment is the read count of one phylum in the reconstructed table. It answers how the phylum composition differs between samples.
    How to read: compare the heights of the same colour across bars. A phylum that dominates one sample but not the others is worth a look at the sample metadata.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: count
    color: Phylum
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      count: Reads
      Phylum: Phylum

- component: figure
  title: Composition by genus
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and each segment is the read count of one genus in the reconstructed table. It answers which genera drive the differences between samples.
    How to read: the reconstruction resolves finer ranks than a single region does, so genus level is meaningful here. Many segments in a bar mean a diverse sample.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: count
    color: Genus
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      count: Reads
      Genus: Genus

- component: card
  title: Reconstructed features
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct reconstructed features, and the bars rank the phyla that hold most of them. It answers how rich the reconstructed community is.
    How to read: the secondary number counts feature and sample rows. A feature found in few samples is rare, so check its confidence in the reconstruction tab.
  column: feature_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: Phylum
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: features, by phylum
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples in the table, and the bars rank the samples by the number of feature rows they hold. It answers how many samples were reconstructed and how rich each is.
    How to read: a sample with far fewer rows than the others had less depth or lost features during reconstruction.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: rows, by sample

- component: card
  title: Phyla
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct phyla, and the bar shows each phylum's share of the feature rows. It answers how broad the community is and whether a few phyla dominate.
    How to read: a bar mostly made of one phylum means a community with low evenness at this rank.
  column: Phylum
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: Phylum
  caption: rows, by phylum

- component: interactive
  title: Phylum
  description: |-
    Pick one or more phyla to keep. It filters every tile of the tab to the features of those phyla.
    How to read: pick one phylum to see its genera in the composition bars.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: Phylum

- component: table
  title: Reconstructed features table
  description: |-
    Each row is a feature in a sample with its read count, full lineage and the rank columns. It answers exactly what was found and in how many reads.
    How to read: sort by count, or filter by phylum or genus to find a taxon.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: reconstruction_support
  title: Region coverage against kmer support
  description: |-
    Each point is a reconstructed feature: the number of amplified regions that mapped to it on the horizontal axis and the kmer support summed over them on the vertical axis. The size is the mean support per region and the colour its spread across regions. It answers how well each feature is backed by the sequenced regions.
    How to read: a point to the right is carried by several regions and is a stronger claim than one carried by a single region. A high point with an uneven colour has most of its support in one region. Follow up the labelled points in the table.
    Note: q2-sidle publishes no minimum number of regions or kmers, so no cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://q2-sidle.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reconstruction.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: stdv_kmer_per_region
    x_title: Regions mapped
    y_title: Kmers mapped
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    x: num_regions
    y: total_kmers_mapped
    size: mean_kmer_per_region
    label: feature_id

- component: figure
  title: Features by regions mapped
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the reconstructed features that were mapped by a given number of amplified regions. It answers how many features rest on one region and how many on all of them.
    How to read: a distribution piled on the highest value means the regions agree and the reconstruction is well supported. A tall bar at one region means many features are single-region claims.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: num_regions
    labels:
      num_regions: Regions mapped
      count: Features

- component: card
  title: Regions per feature
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average count of amplified regions that mapped to a feature, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how much cross-region support the features have.
    How to read: the closer it is to the number of regions sequenced, the more complete the reconstruction. A low value means most features come from a single region.
  column: num_regions
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Kmer support
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median total kmer support per feature, and the histogram shows its distribution. It answers how much sequence evidence stands behind a typical feature.
    How to read: a long right tail is normal. Features at the lowest values are the weakest reconstructions, so look at them in the table first.
  column: total_kmers_mapped
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: median, with its range

- component: card
  title: Kmers per region
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average kmer support per mapped region, and the histogram shows its distribution over features. It answers how deep the support is on each region and not only in total.
    How to read: a value near one means each region adds little evidence by itself. Higher values mean regions that pin the feature down.
  column: mean_kmer_per_region
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: average, with its range

- component: table
  title: Reconstruction confidence table
  description: |-
    Each row is a reconstructed feature with the number of regions mapped, the kmer support and the per-region ASVs behind it. It answers which features are well supported.
    How to read: sort by regions mapped, then by kmer support.
